political_impact.text: The Agriculture Department appointed Paul Kroegel warden of the new reservation in a letter of April 4, 1903.
political_impact.source: The Auk, January 1904 (Dutcher, A.O.U. committee report)

legacy.text: Pelican Island, the first federal bird reservation, became the seed of the National Wildlife Refuge System.
The Biological Survey's own register lists Pelican Island as reservation No. 1, established March 14, 1903.

related.note: The 1909 enlargement order, whose recital (followed by Lord) gives the original order's date as March 13.

uncertain: The date rests on contemporary records saying March 14, 1903, against the March 13 recited in Executive Order 1014; the signed original in National Archives Record Group 11 has not been examined.

legacy.text: Breton Island was the second federal bird reservation, and Lord's listing under October 4, 1904 settles an old conflict between 1904 and 1905.
legacy.source: Lord, List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders, Unnumbered Series

political_impact.text: Almost none of the unnumbered orders drew notice on its own; they were routine acts that mattered to the clerk, officer or land district they touched.

legacy.text: Lord's index shows that numbered and unnumbered orders cover the same fields; whether an order got a number depended only on whether the State Department had a copy on file in 1907.
legacy.source: Lord, List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders, Unnumbered Series, preface

legacy.text: Once numbered orders listed twice are netted out, Lord's 126 Roosevelt entries yield 105 distinct unnumbered orders, well above the often-repeated estimate of about 75.
